President Donald Trump pushed back Monday on questions about whether his administration’s deportation policy had gone too far, reaffirming a hardline approach and ruling out amnesty even as he elevated the policy’s chief architect to White House chief of staff.   During an impromptu White House briefing room appearance on November 9, CBS News chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes pressed Trump on comments he made in a “60 Minutes” interview that aired the previous day. In that sit-down, Trump said his deportation efforts “might be too tough” and acknowledged they had hurt him politically after Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate in the midterms. He suggested openness to working with the new Democratic majority on some form of immigration deal that could allow certain long-term undocumented workers to remain.   Cordes noted that shortly after the interview was taped, Trump named Stephen Miller, widely described as the architect of the administration’s aggressive enforcement strategy, as his new chief of staff. She asked whether Trump had directed Miller to make changes to the deportation policy.   Trump responded directly: “We have a very strong deportation policy. There’s no amnesty, no, no anything. We keep that. But we focus on the worst of the worst.” He added that the priority remains removing “murderers” and other serious offenders, stating, “We’ve gotten most of them out.” He repeated long-standing claims that the Biden administration had allowed roughly 25 million people into the country, including “11,888 murderers, most of whom committed more than one murder,” along with people from prisons and mental institutions in countries including the Congo, across South America, and Asia. “What Biden did to this country should never, ever be forgotten,” he said.   Trump also acknowledged that many people who entered illegally now hold jobs, are productive, and in some cases pay taxes, but he maintained there would be no amnesty. The exchange highlights a mixed message in the days after the midterm losses.   Source: @CBSNews #lunionsuite #haitianamerican #haitian
